title: A class of site coverings admits a set of representatives with prescribed coverings
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category whose objects and arrows form sets. Let $\operatorname{Cov}$ be a possibly proper class of set-indexed families of arrows with a common target, satisfying the three covering axioms of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1), without the requirement that the collection of families be a set: every singleton isomorphism is in $\operatorname{Cov}$; composites of a family in $\operatorname{Cov}$ with families in $\operatorname{Cov}$ on each of its domains are in $\operatorname{Cov}$; and for any family in $\operatorname{Cov}$ and any arrow to its target all the required fibre products exist and the pulled-back family is in $\operatorname{Cov}$. For every set $\operatorname{Cov}_0\subseteq\operatorname{Cov}$ there is a set $\operatorname{Cov}'$ with $\operatorname{Cov}_0\subseteq\operatorname{Cov}'\subseteq\operatorname{Cov}$ satisfying the same three axioms, such that every family in $\operatorname{Cov}$ is combinatorially equivalent to a family in $\operatorname{Cov}'$. Here combinatorially equivalent means that the two families have the same target and the same set of arrows, ignoring repetitions.

source.place: Tag 000X (sets-lemma-coverings-site), clauses (1)-(3); hypotheses and combinatorial equivalence in Section 000W

proof.text: Use the small type of pairs (X,R), where X is an object and R is a presieve on X. Take its subtype of pairs realized by some family in Cov, and use Choice to select one such family for each realized pair. The range of this choice map is small, is contained in Cov, and represents every family with exactly the same target and presieve. Including the target separately handles empty families. This is the proved private lemma exists_small_covering_representatives.

source.place: Tag 000X (lemma-coverings-site), first paragraph; target included to cover empty supports; Collection replaces the equivalent least-rank witness construction

proof.text: For the closure lemma, work inside the subtype A of families in Cov. The initial small subset B_0 consists of the prescribed families and the singleton isomorphisms; the latter are the image of the small type of pairs of objects and isomorphism arrows. The cardinalities of the initial index types have a common bound because their range is small. Enlarge the bound to an infinite cardinal kappa. For compositions, Cardinal.mk_sigma and Cardinal.sum_le_sum bound the new index cardinal by |I| times kappa, and Cardinal.mul_eq_self gives kappa times kappa = kappa. This uses direct infinite-cardinal arithmetic in place of the finite-list argument.

source.place: Tag 000X (lemma-coverings-site), second paragraph, infinite cardinal arithmetic; Tag 000D (section-cardinals)

proof.text: Set theta to the initial ordinal of the successor cardinal of kappa. Mathlib Cardinal.isRegular_succ gives regularity of that successor cardinal, so its le_cof_ord field gives kappa < cf(theta). Cardinal.isSuccLimit_ord shows theta is a nonzero limit ordinal. These are the Mathlib form of the large-cofinality argument of Sets Tag 05N3.

For a small S contained in A, let T(S) contain S, every indexed composition with outer and inner families in S, and one chosen covering pullback of each family in S along each arrow to its target. Choose pullback data from the proved hypothesis IsCoveringClass Cov, retaining the original index type. Each fixed-target fiber of S injects into S. Thus the composition parameters form a small dependent sum of dependent function types, the pullback parameters form a small dependent sum, and T(S) is small. The index-cardinality bound kappa is preserved by T. Using WellFoundedLT.fix, define B_alpha = B_0 union the union of T(B_beta) over beta < alpha. Well-founded induction proves smallness and the cardinal bound at every stage. Since T contains its argument, the stages are monotone and T(B_alpha) is contained in B_beta whenever alpha < beta. These are fully proved private helpers.

source.place: Tag 000X (lemma-coverings-site), transfinite closure construction; direct sets of families in place of rank cutoffs

proof.text: Let S be the union of B_alpha for alpha < theta, and let Cov_prime be its image under the subtype inclusion A into all families. Smallness follows from smallness of the type of ordinals below theta and of every stage. Cov_prime contains the prescribed families and singleton isomorphisms and is contained in Cov. A family in S lies in some B_alpha with alpha < theta; its chosen covering pullback lies in T(B_alpha), hence in B_(alpha+1), still below theta because theta is a limit. The chosen pullback data supply exactly the pullback-existence clause of IsCoveringClass, without claiming closure under other choices.

For a composite, choose a stage alpha for its outer family and a stage beta_i for every inner family. The index set has cardinal at most kappa < cf(theta), so Ordinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof gives sup_i beta_i < theta, also for empty index sets. Set delta = max(alpha, sup_i beta_i). Monotonicity puts the outer family and every inner family in B_delta, and their composite is in T(B_delta), hence in B_(delta+1) and S. This proves the closure lemma exists_small_covering_closure. Finally apply that lemma to the union of Cov_0 and the representatives R from step 1. Inclusion of R transports its exact-presieve representatives into Cov_prime and proves the final clause of the theorem.

source.place: Tag 000X (lemma-coverings-site), final paragraph and condition (3); repair beta<beta_1 to beta<beta_2 and include the outer stage

proof_origin.place: Tag 000X and Tag 05N3; complete Lean proof by S3, 2026-10-16. Direct small-stage closure with WellFoundedLT.fix; direct infinite-cardinal multiplication and regularity of the successor cardinal replace the finite-list detour and the expanded cofinality argument. Public statement and unit route unchanged.
